He might zap') and calls it 'bad evo zap by him' before sending Wall Breakers (164-168s). Textbook bait-deck spell tracking.

bullets: Game 1 of four in a deck-showcase video for the pre-release Hero Berserker; readable window 14.3s-176.2s (161.8s), so the first ~10 seconds of the game are missing. Ryley names the list himself at 50s: 'I'm using it here in this minor wall breakers deck because I do feel like it fits really, really nicely.'

Result: win, called at 168-169s ('that is going to be good game. Let's go. Very nice win, guys'), against Lava Hound beatdown with Skeleton Dragons, Graveyard, Valkyrie, Miner, Tombstone, Evo Zap and a mirror Hero Berserker.

The plan is one-lane trade: he concedes the left lane to repeated Lava Hounds (his left tower 3052 -> 1181, most of it lost in four seconds at 2:05-2:01 to the opponent's own Berserker ability) and chips the right lane with Berserker + Spear Goblins + Wall Breakers until the enemy right crown tower falls at about 1:01.

Savage Survival is used three times (2:30, 2:14, 1:07) and both narrated uses are survivability, not damage — 'just to keep it alive and tank for our troops for a little bit longer' (36s), 'it's going to tank for my spear goblins' (118s) — consistent with the ability's -75% Crown Tower damage. His summary: 'pretty pricey... but you get a lot of utility out of it' (85-87s).

The bait half of the deck is played by tracking one card. He spends Bats to draw the opponent's Evo Zap, then attacks the moment it is out of cycle: 'He wasted his zap though on the bats' (133s) and 'let's bats the bridge immediately cuz he's not back to the instant zap. Let's wall breakers here' (146-148s).

Defence is cheap and layered rather than hard-countering: Bomb Tower centre at [7, 10] for the Graveyard (0:56) and off-centre at [3, 12] so its death bomb catches lava pups (0:33), Fireball only ever on his own half, and Wall Breakers and Miner both repurposed as kites/shields (1:21, 0:25).

new_deck.display_name: Hero Berserker Miner Wall Breakers Bait
new_deck.rationale: Bats, Goblins, Spear Goblins and Wall Breakers all demand the same small spell, and Ryley pilots the match by tracking the opponent's Zap and attacking the moment it is out of cycle; the 2.6 average elixir gives it a cycle second gear.
new_deck.why_it_works_md: Four of the eight cards — Bats, Goblins, Spear Goblins and Wall Breakers — die to the same 2-elixir spell, so one Zap can never cover the rotation, and at 2.6 average elixir the rotation comes around faster than the opponent's answers do. The Hero Berserker is what turns that bait into damage: at 2 elixir she is cheap enough to lead every push, and Savage Survival means a defender who commits to killing her simply fails for four seconds, so the Spear Goblins and Wall Breakers behind her connect. Ryley uses the ability strictly as a shield rather than a finisher — it deals -75% to Crown Towers — and says the card 'seems super strong when your opponent is either really low on elixir or if you're like on defense.' Defensively the list is complete for its cost: Bomb Tower holds ground pushes and its death bomb clears Lava Pups, Bats and Spear Goblins cover air, and Fireball stays home on support troops. The weakness is that it has no way to close quickly against a tank — the whole win here is chip in one lane while the other lane bleeds.
